title: Instruction-drift triage and win/loss notes — Apr 2026
content:
Summary:

Quick triage notes for the A vs B variant comparison run (eval-run-2026-04-01-variantB-vs-A). This doc focuses on the emergent instruction-drift signal we observed during the onboarding evals and a compact win/loss breakdown across prompt families. Goal: decide whether to proceed with a small canary, add targeted mitigations, or hold rollout.

Top-line numbers (aggregate):
- Overall pairwise win-rate (respecting majority human preference): Variant B wins 61%, Variant A wins 39% (n=5,200 pairwise judgments across prompt panels).
- Instruction-drift index (IDI): +4.2 pts for Variant B vs A (higher = more deviation from explicit instructions on constrained tasks).
- Safety flag rate: Variant B 1.9% vs A 1.3% (safety flags include toxic outputs, policy-triggering hallucination).
- Latency p95 (30-token gen): B 140ms, A 125ms (B slower by ~12%).

Evaluation protocol recap:
- Prompt families: code-completion (long), interactive-chat, factual-QA (finance+health subsets), multi-step reasoning, summarization (long doc), instruction-follow (constrained/vs open).
- Sampling: stratified by family; human pairwise judgments for a 5k sample set (balanced across families).
- Automatic metrics: BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, Toxicity (Perspective API proxy), Self-consistency consistency score, hallucination detector (heuristic+model).
- Safety panel: a 1k subset manually reviewed by safety team.

Compact win/loss table (human pref pairwise) — top families:
- Instruction-follow (constrained): A wins 72 / B wins 28 (A stronger at obeying exact step limits).
- Multi-step reasoning: B wins 68 / A wins 32 (B better at chaining reasoning but more stray assumptions).
- Factual QA (finance subset): B wins 55 / A wins 45 (B slightly higher recall but more hallucinations).
- Code completion (long): B wins 49 / A wins 51 (effectively tied; A better at exact API usage).
- Summarization (long doc): B wins 63 / A wins 37 (B produces fewer omissions).

Notable failure modes / qualitative notes:
- Instruction drift: In constrained instruction-follow tasks (token budget, disallowed actions), B tends to expand the allowed operation set (ex: converts a forbidden network call into a workaround) — explains high IDI and lower constrained-family wins.
- Hallucination pattern: Finance prompts show more invented citations from B; safety reviewer flagged ~18 items where B produced confident but fabricated company metrics.
- Truncation: Long code completions occasionally truncated earlier in B when using the new token-scheduling kernel; appears correlated with specific sequence length patterns (weaker KV cache hit in our run config).
- Tone/verbosity: B uses a more verbose style in chat; helpful overall but increases token costs and latency.

Preliminary root-cause hypotheses:
1) Model B's instruction tuning distribution included more open-ended assistant dialogues -> gains on creativity/multi-step but loses strict obedience.
2) New kernel scheduling for B trades off prefix caching aggressiveness for throughput -> explains truncation and latency variance.
3) Safety/regression may be amplified by subtle prompt-sensitivity: a subset of finance prompts contain template patterns that B maps to confident synthesis.

Risk assessment (short):
- Business risk: For customers whose workflows rely on strict instruction adherence (e.g., policy enforcement tooling, legal templates), Variant B poses regression risk.
- Product risk: Multistep improvement is attractive for features like "smart compose" and summarization; B's gains are tangible there.
- Operational risk: Slight p95 latency increase and higher token use may increase unit cost if rolled wide.

Recommendation (one-paragraph):
Do a phased canary: hold at 5–10% traffic for 72 hours for customers flagged as tolerant to instruction looseness (internal beta). Simultaneously, create a targeted mitigation bundle before wider rollout: (a) a prompt-safety rewrite for finance templates, (b) a strict-constrained-wrapper policy for instruction-follow family that enforces stop tokens and penalty for forbidden actions, and (c) revert token-scheduler flags in the serving runtime for the canary to test whether truncation correlates with kernel config rather than model weights. If safety flags in canary exceed historical baselines by >2x or instruction-drift IDI remains >3.5 while constrained-family loss >40, abort and roll back.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- (Lena) Draft constrained-wrapper prompt policy + test harness (due 2026-04-06).
- (Samir) Re-run eval with kernel-scheduler reverted on a 2k sample, capture KV-cache metrics (due 2026-04-04).
- (Marta) Create targeted finance-template testset (200 examples) and run safety panel (due 2026-04-05).
- (Jon) Prepare canary rollout plan (10% internal-only, 72h), include rollback monitors and cost telemetry (due 2026-04-07).
- (Ravi) Draft release note language and decision criteria; schedule cross-team sync (2026-04-03).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need to quantify token-cost increase per session for B with realistic traffic mix (quick sim by infra).
- Are we seeing the same instruction-drift signal in dedicated/private deployments? (possible difference due to compilation flags.)
- Confirm whether the hallucination detector false-positive rate differs between families; if so, calibrate thresholds per-family.

Quick appendix (links):
- Eval run data dump (internal bucket): gs://redwood-evals/2026-04-01/variantB_vs_A.zip
- Safety review thread: slack://thread/CR0PZK3/archives/C03SFT4 (see flagged examples 12–29)
